scene1_intro_vector_arrow.display_text: Here we treat a 2D vector as an arrow: its length is the magnitude, and its angle θ gives the direction.
scene1_intro_vector_arrow.llm_text: Here we treat a two D vector as an arrow: its length is the magnitude, and its angle theta gives the direction.
scene1_intro_vector_arrow.spoken_text: Here we treat a two D vector as an arrow: its length is the magnitude, and its angle theta gives the direction.

scene1_show_trig_triangle.display_text: To connect geometry to physics, we resolve the vector into perpendicular components: a horizontal component vx and a vertical component vy.
scene1_show_trig_triangle.llm_text: To connect geometry to physics, we resolve the vector into perpendicular components: a horizontal component v x and a vertical component v y.
scene1_show_trig_triangle.spoken_text: To connect geometry to physics, we resolve the vector into perpendicular components: a horizontal component v x and a vertical component v y.

scene1_reveal_components_vx_vy.display_text: The component arrows show how vx = v cosθ and vy = v sinθ. Adding the two components reconstructs the original vector.
scene1_reveal_components_vx_vy.llm_text: The component arrows show how v x equals v cos theta and v y equals v sin theta. Adding the two components reconstructs the original vector.
scene1_reveal_components_vx_vy.spoken_text: The component arrows show how v x equals v cos theta and v y equals v sin theta. Adding the two components reconstructs the original vector.

scene2_intro_tip_to_tail.display_text: Vector addition works by placing vectors head-to-tail. We start with A, then reposition B so its tail meets the head of A.
scene2_intro_tip_to_tail.llm_text: Vector addition works by placing vectors head-to-tail. We start with A, then reposition B so its tail meets the head of A.
scene2_intro_tip_to_tail.spoken_text: Vector addition works by placing vectors head-to-tail. We start with A, then reposition B so its tail meets the head of A.

scene2_connect_head_tail.display_text: Now slide B so its tail coincides with the head of A. The connector line marks the connection rule.
scene2_connect_head_tail.llm_text: Now slide B so its tail coincides with the head of A. The connector line marks the connection rule.
scene2_connect_head_tail.spoken_text: Now slide B so its tail coincides with the head of A. The connector line marks the connection rule.

scene2_show_resultant_R.display_text: The resultant R is the vector from A’s original tail to B’s new head. It’s the single arrow that replaces the two.
scene2_show_resultant_R.llm_text: The resultant R is the vector from A’s original tail to B’s new head. It’s the single arrow that replaces the two.
scene2_show_resultant_R.spoken_text: The resultant R is the vector from A’s original tail to B’s new head. It’s the single arrow that replaces the two.

scene3_intro_decomposition.display_text: Split the launch velocity into horizontal vx and vertical vy components. Horizontal motion stays uniform; vertical motion accelerates due to gravity.
scene3_intro_decomposition.llm_text: Split the launch velocity into horizontal v x and vertical v y components. Horizontal motion stays uniform; vertical motion accelerates due to gravity.
scene3_intro_decomposition.spoken_text: Split the launch velocity into horizontal v x and vertical v y components. Horizontal motion stays uniform; vertical motion accelerates due to gravity.

scene3_apex_and_vy_zero.display_text: As the projectile rises, vy decreases toward zero. At maximum height, vy = 0; then it reverses and grows downward.
scene3_apex_and_vy_zero.llm_text: As the projectile rises, v y decreases toward zero. At maximum height, v y equals zero; then it reverses and grows downward.
scene3_apex_and_vy_zero.spoken_text: As the projectile rises, v y decreases toward zero. At maximum height, v y equals zero; then it reverses and grows downward.

scene3_descending_vy_downwards.display_text: After the apex, vx remains unchanged while vy rotates downward and increases in magnitude—this combination produces the parabolic trajectory.
scene3_descending_vy_downwards.llm_text: After the apex, v x remains unchanged while v y rotates downward and increases in magnitude—this combination produces the parabolic trajectory.
scene3_descending_vy_downwards.spoken_text: After the apex, v x remains unchanged while v y rotates downward and increases in magnitude—this combination produces the parabolic trajectory.

scene4_compare_angles_intro.display_text: Compare two launches with the same speed but different angles. Higher angles increase time aloft and maximum height; lower angles favor range.
scene4_compare_angles_intro.llm_text: Compare two launches with the same speed but different angles. Higher angles increase time aloft and maximum height; lower angles favor range.
scene4_compare_angles_intro.spoken_text: Compare two launches with the same speed but different angles. Higher angles increase time aloft and maximum height; lower angles favor range.

scene4_show_trial2_and_outcomes.display_text: Overlay Trial 2. Look for the landing point (range) and the highest point (maximum height). For fixed speed, an intermediate angle produces maximum range.
scene4_show_trial2_and_outcomes.llm_text: Overlay Trial 2. Look for the landing point (range) and the highest point (maximum height). For fixed speed, an intermediate angle produces maximum range.
scene4_show_trial2_and_outcomes.spoken_text: Overlay Trial 2. Look for the landing point (range) and the highest point (maximum height). For fixed speed, an intermediate angle produces maximum range.

scene4_compare_speeds_low_vs_high.display_text: Now increase launch speed. Both vx and vy components become larger, so the projectile reaches a higher peak and lands farther away.
scene4_compare_speeds_low_vs_high.llm_text: Now increase launch speed. Both v x and v y components become larger, so the projectile reaches a higher peak and lands farther away.
scene4_compare_speeds_low_vs_high.spoken_text: Now increase launch speed. Both v x and v y components become larger, so the projectile reaches a higher peak and lands farther away.
